newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihyaku Life to cut domestic stock holdings.
newsitem.headline: Daihyaku Life to cut domestic stock holdings.

text.p: Daihyaku Mutual Life Insurance Co plans to continue cutting its holdings of domestic stocks in the 1997/98 fiscal year, a company official said on Tuesday.

Three years ago the company began reducing the weighting of domestic stock holdings in its portfolio, which fell to 15.8 percent in fiscal 1996/97, which ended on March 31, from 20.7 percent in fiscal 1994/95.
He added that the company would maintain a flexible stance regarding its investments in foreign securities.
The company held 73.77 billion yen worth of bad loans and problem loans at the end of March, versus total assets of 3.32 trillion yen, he said.
